parsed.explanation: No criminalisation, no documented police targeting, and top-court rulings favouring trans people (2019/2023 bathroom damages; surgery requirement struck) show rule of law working FOR trans visitors. Guidance records little direct hostility, especially in tourist areas. Deductions: no anti-discrimination statute (recourse via litigation only), gender-segregated bathing documented as a real friction though alternatives exist and no bar rule is sourced, custody following the family register with documented misplacement and hormone denial — a serious tier-1-adjacent exposure if a visitor were detained, though the record frames it as resident-facing and no visitor case appears. Foreign document handling can break down (2018 ward refusal, single instance). The 2009 report is a dated baseline. Overall: functional institutions, moderate friction, no universal visitor-facing exclusion documented — reduced risk, but not the acceptance-plus-enforcement tier.
